subject: AWS Marketplace: Fulfillment webhooks, escrow account & usage hooks for Nimbus Analytics
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Lee <amlee@amazon.com>, marketplace-tech@amazon.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Marketplace: Fulfillment webhooks, escrow account & usage hooks for Nimbus Analytics

Hi Amanda / Marketplace team,

Following up from last week's co-sell sync — Nimbus Analytics (prospect) is ready to finalize SaaS listing & procurement. Before we sign, we need to align on three integration items that are blocking legal/procurement:

1) Fulfillment/webhook flows: we need the official AWS expectations for provider-initiated vs. marketplace-initiated fulfillment and the exact webhook payloads AWS will post so we can map entitlement IDs to our internal tenant IDs.
2) Escrow / payout timing: Nimbus has a custom billing cadence and is asking whether AWS will hold funds for 30 days for usage disputes. If there are escrow requirements (or recommended P&L mapping), we need that documented for our finance team.
3) Usage hooks and test harness: we prefer to do provider metering with usage hooks (server-to-server). Please confirm the recommended test account and whether the Marketplace sandbox supports incremental usage reports for SaaS products.

I've attached a short proposed SLA amendment we plan to include in the contract ("proposed-sla-amendment.pdf") and a lightweight sketch of the mapping we need.

Can you confirm who on your side owns the fulfillment webhook contract language and the technical test account (sandbox)? Jonathan Price from Nimbus is on cc and is expecting a short PO / DocuSign amendment once these items are confirmed.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0182

Attachment: proposed-sla-amendment.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Amanda Lee <amlee@amazon.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: marketplace-tech@amazon.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: Fulfillment webhooks, escrow account & usage hooks for Nimbus Analytics

Hi Kimberly — thanks for the clear list. Amanda from AWS Marketplace here. Short answers and next steps below.

1) Fulfillment/webhook flows: AWS supports both provider-initiated and marketplace-initiated fulfillment for SaaS SaaS contracts. For Nimbus we recommend provider-initiated metering (PublishUsage API) with a delivery confirmation webhook so you can reconcile entitlement IDs. The official payload we send for entitlement notifications is attached (aws-saas-fulfillment-guide.pdf), section 4.2 — see "ENTITLEMENT_UPDATE" payload.

2) Escrow / payout: AWS payouts are subject to the AWS Marketplace payout schedule. There isn't a general escrow holding pattern for standard SaaS listings; disputes are handled through the normal billing dispute process. That said, for enterprise procurements we can support a 30-day hold by exception if both parties sign an amendment and AWS Seller Support creates a hold in the payout flow. We'd need legal signoff and a DocuSign envelope.

3) Test harness: we will provision a Marketplace sandbox account that supports PublishUsage and simulated webhook delivery. Provisioning typically takes 2 business days after we receive your seller account ID. I'll loop in Marketplace Technical to coordinate the sandbox and a test harness.

Next steps/action items:
- Amanda: provision sandbox and send test buyer + Sandbox credentials (ETA 48 hours).
- Kimberly / Redwood: confirm the internal entitlement -> tenant mapping (sample IDs is fine).
- Ben: confirm accounting contact for payout hold request.

Attaching the AWS SaaS Fulfillment guide and the sample payloads.

Best,
Amanda Lee
AWS Marketplace Partner Development
amlee@amazon.com

Attachment: aws-saas-fulfillment-guide.pdf (PDF, 210KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Lee <amlee@amazon.com>, marketplace-tech@amazon.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: Fulfillment webhooks, escrow account & usage hooks for Nimbus Analytics

Hi Amanda — thanks, this is helpful. A few technical confirmations from our side and a small ask about signature validation: 

1) Endpoint & TLS: Our preferred endpoint for AWS webhooks will be:
   https://ingest.redwood.com/integrations/aws/marketplace/webhook
   We'll provide a dedicated TLS cert and support mTLS if required.

2) Payload fields: Please include both entitlement_id and customer_reference in the notification. We map entitlement_id -> internal_tenant_id and customer_reference is helpful for quicker reconciliation. Example we expect in the payload (pseudo):

   {
     "eventType": "ENTITLEMENT_UPDATE",
     "entitlement_id": "ent-8a7c-1234",
     "customer_reference": "nimbus-tenant-4711",
     "timestamp": "2027-08-03T22:34:00Z",
     "details": { "plan": "pro", "seats": 12 }
   }

3) Signing / replay protection: We'll validate a signature header (AWS-Signature) on the webhook and require a monotonic nonce/timestamp. If you have a recommended HMAC secret flow, send the key exchange steps.

4) Test harness: Once Amanda provisions the sandbox, we'll run the following acceptance tests:
   - Receive and validate ENTITLEMENT_UPDATE webhook (happy path)
   - Simulate repeated PublishUsage calls and ensure idempotency is preserved
   - Check that entitlement -> tenant mapping is correct for 100 sample IDs

I've attached a tiny sample cert and a YAML sketch of the usage hooks we plan to use (proposed-usage-hooks.yaml).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Runtime Integration | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: sample-webhook-ssl.pem (PEM, 1.2KB); proposed-usage-hooks.yaml (YAML, 3KB)

- Karthik: we'll stand up the webhook endpoint and share the HMAC secret via the secure exchange you prefer.
- Ben / Marissa: please prepare the finance justification for the 30-day payout hold and we will send the DocuSign amendment if AWS confirms they can create the exception.

If all parties agree, we aim to have the sandbox acceptance tests complete by 2027-08-12 and DocuSign signed by 2027-08-15. Jonathan — can you confirm you have purchase approval to sign the amendment on or before 8/15?

I'll follow up with a short mutual action plan doc and will forward the DocuSign envelope once AWS confirms the payout hold escalation path. DocuSign link will be shared to Jonathan's email; I've added the expected envelope URL to the related links.

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick coordination.

Best,
